```{python}
#| label: setup
import hashlib
import json
import platform
import subprocess
from importlib.metadata import version
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import yaml
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

cfg = yaml.safe_load(Path("config/config.yaml").read_text())
res = Path(cfg["results"])
summary = json.loads((res / "summary.json").read_text())
scores = pd.read_csv(res / "scores.csv")
weights = pd.read_csv(res / "view_weights.csv")
data, pcc = summary["data"], summary["pcc_deg"]

STAGES = {"backbone": "Backbone", "first_stage": "+ compound terms", "final": "UnDetect (+ context gate)"}
SPLITS = {"train": "Training", "valid": "Validation", "test": "Test"}
VIEWS = {"chem": "Structure", "tgt": "Targets", "moa": "Mechanism of action", "morph": "Cell Painting"}
COLOUR = {"train": "#c3c2b7", "valid": "#8ec5ea", "test": "#2a78d6", "ink": "#52514e", "grid": "#e4e3df"}
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 9, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False})
f3 = lambda x: f"{x:.3f}"  # noqa: E731
test = {s: pcc[s]["test"] for s in pcc}
```

## Summary

This report comes from one run of the pipeline. UnDetect [@lei2027undetect] predicts how the expression of 978
genes changes when a compound treats a cell line, for compounds the model has never seen. Trained and tested in five
folds on simulated data, it reached a test PCC~DEG~ of `{python} f3(test["final"]["mean"])` (standard deviation
`{python} f3(test["final"]["sd"])` over folds), against `{python} f3(test["backbone"]["mean"])` for its drug-free
backbone alone and a ceiling of `{python} f3(test["ceiling"]["mean"])` set by the simulated noise.

## Data

```{python}
#| label: tbl-data
#| tbl-cap: "The simulated data."
pd.DataFrame({"Value": [f"{data['samples']:,}", data["compounds"], data["moa_classes"], data["cell_lines"],
                        data["plates"], data["genes"], data["with_cell_painting"], 5]},
             index=pd.Index(["Samples (compound, cell line, plate)", "Compounds", "Mechanism-of-action classes",
                             "Cell lines", "Assay plates", "Genes", "Compounds with a Cell Painting profile",
                             "Folds"], name=""))
```

The compounds are real: `{python} data["compounds"]` compounds of the CLUE compound table [@clue2020], with their
structures, targets and mechanisms of action. Their Cell Painting profiles and all responses are simulated (seed
`{python} cfg["simulation"]["seed"]`, settings in `config/config.yaml`), so the answer is known: a response is a
context term set by the control profile of the sample's plate, plus a plate effect, plus a compound effect that is
similar for compounds that are similar in structure, targets, mechanism or morphology, plus noise.

Each fold holds out one fifth of the compounds as test compounds and another fifth as validation compounds, which
choose every setting; the model trains on the other three fifths. Every test compound is new to the model.

## Model

UnDetect fits a response in three stages, each building on the one before:

1. **Backbone.** A neural network predicts, from the sample's control profile alone, the response that any compound
   would show there. It sees no compound information.
2. **Compound terms.** Kernel ridge regression over a compound kernel carries the backbone's residuals from the
   training compounds to new ones, once across all cell lines and once per line. The kernel combines the four views
   of a compound (structure, targets, mechanism, Cell Painting), each weighted by how well it aligns with the
   residuals.
3. **Context gate.** A per-gene model on the control profile's principal components rescales the compound terms.

## Results

```{python}
#| label: tbl-scores
#| tbl-cap: "PCC~DEG~ by stage and split: mean ± standard deviation over the five folds. PCC~DEG~ is the Pearson correlation of the measured and predicted response across genes, averaged over samples. The ceiling is the simulated response without its noise."
table = pd.DataFrame(
    {SPLITS[sp]: [f"{pcc[st][sp]['mean']:.3f} ± {pcc[st][sp]['sd']:.3f}" for st in [*STAGES, "ceiling"]]
     for sp in SPLITS},
    index=pd.Index([*STAGES.values(), "Ceiling (noise-free response)"], name="Stage"))
table
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-scores
#| fig-cap: "PCC~DEG~ of each stage of UnDetect on training, validation and test compounds. Bars: mean over the five folds; error bars: standard deviation; dots: single folds; dashed line: the ceiling on test compounds. On training compounds the compound terms are leave-one-compound-out values, so their training scores are not in-sample fits."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart with three groups (backbone, plus compound terms, UnDetect) and three bars per group (training, validation, test PCC_DEG), with error bars, one dot per fold and a dashed horizontal line for the test ceiling."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 3.2))
for i, st in enumerate(STAGES):
    for j, sp in enumerate(SPLITS):
        v = scores[(scores.stage == st) & (scores.split == sp)].pcc_deg.to_numpy()
        x = i + (j - 1) * 0.27
        ax.bar(x, v.mean(), yerr=v.std(ddof=1), width=0.25, color=COLOUR[sp], zorder=2,
               error_kw=dict(ecolor=COLOUR["ink"], elinewidth=0.7, capsize=2))
        ax.scatter(np.full(len(v), x) + np.linspace(-0.06, 0.06, len(v)), v, s=5, color=COLOUR["ink"], zorder=3)
ax.axhline(test["ceiling"]["mean"], color=COLOUR["ink"], lw=0.9, ls="--", zorder=1)
ax.text(2.45, test["ceiling"]["mean"], "ceiling (test)", ha="right", va="bottom", fontsize=7.5, color=COLOUR["ink"])
ax.set_xticks(range(len(STAGES)), list(STAGES.values()))
ax.set_ylabel("PCC$_\\mathrm{DEG}$")
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
ax.grid(axis="y", color=COLOUR["grid"], lw=0.6)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.legend(handles=[Patch(color=COLOUR[sp], label=SPLITS[sp]) for sp in SPLITS], frameon=False, ncol=3,
          loc="upper left", fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The backbone alone reaches a test PCC~DEG~ of `{python} f3(test["backbone"]["mean"])`. The compound terms raise
this to `{python} f3(test["first_stage"]["mean"])` and the context gate to `{python} f3(test["final"]["mean"])`
(@tbl-scores, @fig-scores). At every stage the mean test score is within
`{python} f3(max(abs(pcc[s]["test"]["mean"] - pcc[s]["valid"]["mean"]) for s in STAGES))` of the mean validation
score, on which the settings were chosen. @tbl-folds shows each fold.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-folds
#| tbl-cap: "Each fold: test PCC~DEG~ of each stage, the backbone's training epochs (it stops early on the validation compounds) and the settings chosen on the validation compounds (ridge λ of the kernel regressions; weights g and h of the shared and per-line compound terms)."
folds = pd.DataFrame(summary["folds"]).set_index("fold")
per_fold = scores[scores.split == "test"].pivot(index="fold", columns="stage", values="pcc_deg")
pd.DataFrame({"Backbone": per_fold.backbone.round(3), "+ compound terms": per_fold.first_stage.round(3),
              "UnDetect": per_fold.final.round(3), "Epochs": folds.backbone_epoch, "λ": folds["lambda"],
              "g": folds.g, "h": folds.h}).rename_axis("Fold")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-example
#| fig-cap: "One test sample, the one with the median UnDetect score: measured against predicted change in expression of the 978 genes, for the backbone alone (left) and for UnDetect (right). r is the sample's PCC~DEG~."
#| fig-alt: "Two scatter plots of measured against predicted expression change, one point per gene. The left panel shows the backbone's prediction, the right panel UnDetect's prediction, each with its correlation r."
tests = scores[(scores.split == "test") & (scores.stage == "final")]
fold_scores = {f: pd.read_csv(res / "folds" / f"fold_{f}" / "scores.csv") for f in tests.fold}
per_sample = pd.concat([d.loc[d.split == "test", ["sample", "final"]].assign(fold=f) for f, d in fold_scores.items()])
pick = per_sample.sort_values("final").iloc[len(per_sample) // 2]
pred = np.load(res / "folds" / f"fold_{int(pick.fold)}" / "test_predictions.npz")
row = int(np.flatnonzero(pred["sample"] == pick["sample"])[0])
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6.4, 3.0), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, key, title in zip(axes, ("backbone", "final"), ("Backbone", "UnDetect")):
    y, p = pred["measured"][row], pred[key][row]
    ax.scatter(p, y, s=4, alpha=0.5, color=COLOUR["test"] if key == "final" else COLOUR["ink"], linewidths=0)
    ax.set_title(f"{title}: r = {np.corrcoef(y, p)[0, 1]:.2f}", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel("Predicted change")
    ax.grid(color=COLOUR["grid"], lw=0.6)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
axes[0].set_ylabel("Measured change")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

UnDetect weighs the four compound views by their alignment with the residual responses of the training compounds.
@fig-weights sets these learned weights next to the weights used in the simulation. Alignment measures how well a
view's kernel on its own matches the residuals; it is not an estimate of the simulation's weights, so the two need
not agree.

```{python}
#| label: fig-weights
#| fig-cap: "Weight of each compound view in the simulation and as learned by UnDetect on the training compounds of each fold (mean, error bar: standard deviation over the five folds)."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart for four compound views: structure, targets, mechanism of action and Cell Painting. For each view one hatched bar shows the simulated weight and one solid bar the learned weight, with error bars."
vw = summary["view_weights"]
x = np.arange(len(vw))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.4, 2.8))
ax.bar(x - 0.2, [vw[v]["simulated"] for v in vw], width=0.38, color="white", edgecolor=COLOUR["ink"],
       hatch="////", linewidth=0.8, zorder=2)
ax.bar(x + 0.2, [vw[v]["learned_mean"] for v in vw], yerr=[vw[v]["learned_sd"] for v in vw], width=0.38,
       color=COLOUR["test"], error_kw=dict(ecolor=COLOUR["ink"], elinewidth=0.7, capsize=2), zorder=2)
ax.set_xticks(x, [VIEWS[v].replace(" of ", "\nof ") for v in vw])
ax.set_ylabel("View weight")
ax.grid(axis="y", color=COLOUR["grid"], lw=0.6)
ax.set_axisbelow(True)
ax.legend(handles=[Patch(facecolor="white", edgecolor=COLOUR["ink"], hatch="////", label="simulated"),
                   Patch(color=COLOUR["test"], label="learned")], frameon=False, fontsize=8)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Software

```{python}
#| label: tbl-software
#| tbl-cap: "Main software, read when the report was rendered. Every package comes from the Pixi environment locked in `pixi.lock`."
import rdkit
import torch

quarto = subprocess.run(["quarto", "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
pd.DataFrame({"Version": [platform.python_version(), np.__version__, pd.__version__, torch.__version__,
                          rdkit.__version__, matplotlib.__version__, version("snakemake"), quarto]},
             index=pd.Index(["Python", "NumPy", "pandas", "PyTorch", "RDKit", "Matplotlib", "Snakemake", "Quarto"],
                            name="Software"))
```

Platform: `{python} platform.platform()`; `pixi.lock` SHA-256
`{python} hashlib.sha256(Path("pixi.lock").read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]`. PyTorch ran on the CPU, with at most
`{python} cfg["model"]["epochs"]` training epochs for the backbone.

## Data availability

The CLUE compound table [@clue2020] is downloaded by `scripts/download_data.py`, which checks it against
`metadata/checksums.sha256`; `metadata/sources.tsv` records its source and terms. Everything else is simulated by
`scripts/simulate_data.py` and is regenerated by the pipeline.
